I've had NMS in my library for years. I played it once waaay back after buying it at a price that was almost nil because of the bad luck and press the devs had received starting before 2020. I THINK I played it but it might have been Elite Dangerous (ambitious but .... nah). But it always forced itself on my radar. Then I watched an old (6 YEARS!) episode of Internet Historian on YouTube titled "The Engoodening of No Man's Sky" and as old as it was?  To tell the story It started off rough and then after watching Hello Games almost pushed up a giant & tall tree farmed by press and expectations (and ridiculous deadlines) into awkward and untenable positions as they climbed up and then fall hitting every branch on the way down? My heart felt for them. Having it (humorously) all broken down bit  by bit and everything that led to the fall from a height that they never expected to be at when they were shoved. Then get up, dust themselves off and get back to work making the game they promised with free updates and then go beyond adding more free updates (yes even this year as we recently experienced) for almost a decade after people had completely written NMS sky off? Is an incredible and dedicated come back story that is tribute to the perseverance of everyone at Hello Games making sure their vision and the expectations of the fans (and jilted early owners of NMS) were met and vindicated. And the history I watched (as I said) was 6 years old! Then I saw a new huge update coming for NMS and decided to wait for release and finally PLAY it. I have to say I had to watch a ton of tutorial videos on YouTube (after sifting through the videos that can date up to 10 years old). It was hard catching up as I noticed what huge international player base existed. I still have my questions about certain things large and small that I have to research or just put on hold unless it is a "need to know now" situation involving gameplay or mechanics. So.... is it good? Yes, it is great. Does it have a learning curve involving a buttload of information? Yep. But I am making my way just fine. Still have stop and do research if I can't find it on my phone right away. But therein is the greatness of this game. Making tutorial to a game that is always getting updates is HARD. But getting in the game and "getting caught up" to understanding how to play the current build is worth it. If you are on the fence or have been bored by other space exploration games that were ballyhooed as the next "Big Title" that turn sour? Don't let that or anything else stop you from jumping into No Man's Sky. So much has been endured by other players and so much work has been relentlessly put into this game. Odds are, you will experience that to your enjoyment. 354 hours in, I can safely say that I recommend this game..... Haha!

No Man’s Sky is easily one of the best and most feature-packed space exploration games out there. The sheer amount of content, freedom, and things to discover is absolutely incredible. Whether you want to explore the far reaches of the universe, build an empire, become a space pirate, collect exotic creatures, or simply settle down on a beautiful planet and build a home, this game gives you the freedom to play however you want.

One of the most impressive features is the seamless transition between space and planetary exploration. You can fly directly from space down to a planet's surface without loading screens, fly like a plane through a planet's atmosphere, explore the terrain, and land practically anywhere you want. With the right technology installed, you can even land on water!

And there's no shortage of places to call home. You can build elaborate bases on planets and even underwater bases, construct outposts on massive asteroids, create your own space stations, and even build and customize your own massive freighters, which essentially serve as mobile bases you can take with you across the galaxy. You can also claim abandoned or NPC-operated space stations, renovate them, expand their interiors, and make them your own. If that's not enough, you can take control of planetary settlements and develop them into thriving little cities, making decisions that affect their growth and development.

The sheer scale of the universe in No Man's Sky is almost impossible to comprehend. There are 256 unique galaxies to explore, each containing roughly 4.2 billion star systems per galaxy, with an estimated 18.4 quintillion procedurally generated planets and moons across the universe. That's 18,446,744,073,709,551,616 possible worlds to discover! Each one can have its own landscapes, environments, wildlife, plants, weather conditions, and points of interest. No Man’s Sky’s universe is so unbelievably massive that you could spend your entire lifetime exploring and still barely scratch the surface. You'll never come close to seeing even 1% of its universe.

Exploration is a huge part of the experience. There are countless planets to discover, each with different environments, landscapes, wildlife, plants, weather conditions, and sometimes extremely dangerous hazards. You can discover strange alien creatures, scan plants and animals, uncover ancient ruins, search for buried treasures, explore abandoned facilities, and stumble across all sorts of unusual discoveries. There is also deep-sea exploration, alien ocean life, submarine vehicles and underwater base building. You can even name planets, creatures, and star systems you discover yourself.

Space exploration is also a huge part of the experience, and there's much more to it than simply flying between planets and star systems. You can discover and explore abandoned, procedurally generated derelict freighters drifting through space. These massive ships are filled with dangerous environmental hazards, hostile enemies, valuable loot, and technology waiting to be recovered.

There's also Space Hulk exploration, where you encounter massive abandoned ships that can be dismantled and salvaged for valuable resources, technology modules, and blueprints. Using a gravity gun built into your multitool and a ship-mounted tractor beam, you can literally tear these enormous wrecks apart piece by piece. But it's not without its risks! These operations can be extremely dangerous, as you have limited time to salvage everything before the wreck explodes. You also have to be careful about which sections you remove, because pulling the wrong components can trigger an explosion prematurely. It's a fun, high-risk activity that adds another exciting dimension to space exploration. 

There's also an incredible amount of variety when it comes to missions and activities. The game has numerous questlines, side missions, storylines, and challenges to keep you busy. There are special community events and limited-time Expeditions that introduce unique objectives and challenges, often rewarding you with exclusive ships, cosmetics, decorations, companions, and other items you can bring back to your main save.

Speaking of companions, you can hunt down, adopt, and tame all sorts of alien creatures. You can customize and genetically modify them, even introducing mutations to improve their stats and abilities. You can take them on adventures, use them as companions, and even participate in creature battles against other players and NPCs.

If you prefer a more relaxing experience, there's fishing, too! You can find different types of fish, collect them, and cook them into meals that provide useful buffs. There's also a farming system where you can grow a variety of plants and harvest resources to craft ingredients, create food, and produce valuable items. Cooking itself is surprisingly extensive, with all sorts of recipes to experiment with.

For those who enjoy ships and space combat, there's plenty to get into as well. You can discover, purchase, collect, upgrade, and customize different types of starships, each with its own design and purpose. From nimble fighters and explorers to massive haulers and exotic ships, there's something for everyone. You can engage in space battles, fight pirates, raid cargo fleets, participate in dogfights, and even become a pirate yourself. You can also assemble and command your own fleet of frigates, sending them on expeditions to gather resources and rewards.

One of my favorite features of No Man’s Sky is the incredible ship customization. You're not limited to simply buying ships and upgrading their stats. You can actually salvage and dismantle many of the smaller starships for their individual components, then use those parts to construct and customize your own ships. This allows you to mix and match different components to create a ship with a look and style that's entirely your own.

And then there are Corvettes, which take ship building to an entirely different level. These are much larger, fully customizable ships that you can purchase or build yourself by collecting the necessary parts and components. What makes them especially cool is that they're practically small mobile bases! You can walk around inside them, decorate their interiors, and install useful facilities such as crafting stations, healing stations, and storage. It's almost like having your own personal spaceship that you designed from the ground up.

There are also several different exocraft vehicles you can unlock, build, upgrade and drive across planetary surfaces. These range from fast, nimble vehicles (a bike or buggy) for getting around quickly to larger, more heavily equipped vehicles designed for exploration, combat, and resource gathering. And if exploring on land isn't enough, you can even build and pilot a submarine to explore the depths of those incredibly deep oceans, discovering underwater creatures, resources, and points of interest that you wouldn't otherwise be able to reach.

There's a deep crafting, gathering, and resource-management system that gives you plenty of reasons to explore. Mine resources, refine materials, manufacture technology, upgrade your equipment, improve your multitool, and constantly work toward making your character, ships, and bases better. There's also an extensive trading system, allowing you to buy and sell goods, take advantage of different galactic economies, and build up your wealth.

Multiplayer adds another layer to the experience. You can explore the universe with friends, build bases together, participate in missions, visit other players' creations, and take part in community activities. The game even has a shared social hub (The Space anomaly): A social hub where you can meet other Travelers, access missions, purchase upgrades, and interact with other players and embark on adventures together.

With 150 hours under my belt and the Main quest now at "New Beginnings", I think a review is due.

Started playing a few months ago somewhat on and off; knowing of it's history and the comeback it's made since it's debut. Man is this a great experience. From the base building and resource collecting, to having freighters and space stations. From the Companion Battles to the Corvette building. This game has so much! Even the story while very simple in execution, was very enjoyable with it's message about finding purpose in an infinite universe. As for the main gimmick of the game being the scale of a galaxy with trillions of systems, I can enjoy it's scale and variety. Though there is one negative from this.

Every system and planet is procedurally generated so they should be unique (Which they are technically). But even if they are different, they do sometimes feel the same. Mostly barren planets with the creatures simply having certain assets mixed up. Maybe if there were a few planets every 30 systems that had a decently sized city or 2 on their surface with it's own gimmicks and events. Maybe if the animals had slightly better AI and more unique ways to interact with other than getting food or for Companion battles.

Even with these nitpicks, I still believe that the rest outweighs them. Also, I got this on sale when it's usually $60. It was $24 which was a steal. So it's definitely worth trying it out when they do start these sales. 

If you like space and Base Building games, it's a no brainer. I truly believe this is a comeback story that will go down in history for gaming. Here's to more updates to this huge game.

8.5/10
